title: Upstream fidelity, debugging and reconstruction-tooling maintenance
summary: Review eight material upstream changes across emulation, reconstruction, source-derived ports and retro platform work
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source or target CPU areas, so no architecture value was invented for this pass. Eight materially changed projects were reviewed from primary upstream commits after the prior maintenance receipt. Downland's NABU path is recorded as a proof of concept and CD-i is removed from its supported-platform claim. The tracker did not compile, execute, byte-compare or hardware-test upstream software.

project.status: Active browser and Electron emulator whose debugger now supports reverse-continue to a previous breakpoint or watchpoint, reverse step-out and last-writer lookup; upstream released these changes in 2.18.0, but the tracker did not independently run them.

identity.narrative: The reverse-debugger additions and 2.18.0 release remain features of the canonical jsbeeb BBC Micro-family emulator.

classification.narrative: Reverse execution, memory-write provenance and media inspection reinforce jsbeeb's classification as a core emulator/debugging environment.

source_cpu.narrative: The new debugger traverses recorded state for the already documented MOS 6502/65C02/65C12 models; it introduces no new emulated CPU family.

target_cpu.narrative: Browser and Electron delivery still establishes no fixed native output CPU, so no host ISA is inferred from the TypeScript implementation.

build.narrative: Upstream adds tested reverse-continue, reverse step-out and memory last-writer paths and records known reverse-search gaps. The tracker did not install dependencies, run tests or execute the release.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The existing documented browser and Node.js floors remain; these commits state no new CPU, RAM or OS minimum.

ai.narrative: The reverse-continue commit explicitly attributes generation to Claude Code and co-authorship to Claude Opus 5.5; attribution is limited to the evidenced change.

relationships.narrative: The debugger remains integrated in jsbeeb; no separately titled reverse-debugging project appeared.

project.status: Firestaff now adds a native Apple IIGS melee-action path and parses Macintosh sound and SONG resources while refining authenticated-media candidate reporting; broader native playability and Dungeon Master Nexus completion remain open.

identity.narrative: Apple IIGS combat and Macintosh resource work remain platform paths inside Firestaff's multi-version Dungeon Master/Chaos Strikes Back reconstruction.

classification.narrative: The commits continue bounded clean-room reconstruction from original media, resources and observed behavior rather than claiming recovered source.

source_cpu.narrative: The reviewed Apple IIGS path remains 65C816-related and the Macintosh resource work adds no new source architecture beyond the record's established families.

target_cpu.narrative: The native host outputs remain x86 and arm64 as previously evidenced; parser and gameplay changes do not establish another target CPU.

build.narrative: Upstream implements native Apple IIGS melee dispatch plus Macintosh sound and music resource handling, but these bounded routes do not establish complete playability.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile, execute or compare the new paths against hardware or emulator captures.
build.next_action: Continue bounded native runtime and Nexus gates without converting route-level coverage into a complete-playability claim.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Existing verified profiles remain unchanged; these commits state no new minimum host CPU, RAM, chipset, OS or ROM requirement.

ai.narrative: Existing bounded AI attribution remains applicable to the project; the reviewed functional evidence is limited to the cited commits and no broader authorship claim is made.

relationships.narrative: Apple IIGS and Macintosh implementations remain platform variants within Firestaff rather than separate titled projects.

project.status: Amiga-source-derived SDL2 PC/web port whose editor now supports safer shared-corner editing, discoverable texture painting, native textured FPS editing and floor-material banks while preserving editor camera state across playtests; newly authored full levels remain unproven.

identity.narrative: The FPS editor, texture painting and playtest handoff remain integrated components of Alien Breed HD.

classification.narrative: This remains an Amiga-source-derived C/SDL2 port with an authoring tool, not a decompilation or a newly reverse-engineered original.

source_cpu.narrative: The original Amiga source basis remains Motorola 68000 assembly; editor implementation changes do not alter the source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: Portable desktop/web builds and editor code do not establish one fixed output CPU, so no host ISA is inferred.

build.narrative: Upstream implements guarded shared-corner edits, texture-painting discovery, textured FPS editing, floor-material banks and deterministic return from playtests. The tracker did not build or execute these paths.
build.limitations: Complete newly authored geometry and playable end-to-end new levels remain unverified.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed commits state no minimum host CPU, RAM, GPU, browser or OS version.
runtime_profiles.next_action: Check primary build documentation and qualified releases for concrete minimum desktop/web requirements before adding a runtime profile.

ai.narrative: The reviewed commits contain no explicit development-AI attribution; absence in this bounded evidence is not proof of non-use.

relationships.narrative: The FPS editor and playtest mode remain parts of Alien Breed HD, not separately titled projects.

project.status: PAL 2.00 PS2 reconstruction now replaces thousands of stale shared extern declarations with per-file headers through a checked migration tool; this structural cleanup does not by itself establish additional matching or playability.

identity.narrative: Header migration and declaration cleanup remain within the Ratchet and Clank PAL 2.00 reconstruction.

classification.narrative: The work is source-structure recovery and decompilation hygiene under the existing matching-reconstruction scope.

source_cpu.narrative: The original PS2 Emotion Engine target remains MIPS; declaration migration introduces no new source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The reconstructed PS2 output remains MIPS as previously evidenced; host-side migration tooling is not an output architecture.

build.narrative: Upstream reports moving 372 prototypes into per-file headers and removing 5,729 unused extern declarations with purpose-built tooling. The tracker did not compile or measure matching.
build.limitations: Structural header progress does not independently prove new matching functions or runtime playability.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed commits state no minimum emulator, console, RAM, BIOS or host requirement.

ai.narrative: The main header-migration commit explicitly credits Claude Opus 5.5; attribution is limited to that change.

relationships.narrative: Migration scripts are repository tooling for the same reconstruction, not separate projects.

source_cpu.narrative: The original DOS binary remains x86 as previously evidenced; timing and rendering comparisons do not add another source ISA.

target_cpu.narrative: The SDL port remains portable and the reviewed commits do not establish one fixed output CPU or minimum host ISA.

build.narrative: Upstream corrects shop-return marker timing and rendering order against the town binary oracle and expands pixel-clean cavern/background scenarios. The tracker did not build or replay those comparisons.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed commits provide no minimum host CPU, RAM, OS or SDL requirement.

ai.narrative: The shop-timing commit explicitly records opencode with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash agent; attribution is limited to that commit.

relationships.narrative: Oracle tools and comparison scenarios remain internal validation assets for the same Zeliard project.

project.status: GameCube reconstruction now uses Ghidra/REA-backed drafting, variant search, m2c drafts, finishable-unit ranking and stricter gap workflows while matching additional PS2DMA packet helpers; no independent build or execution was performed.

identity.narrative: The analysis and drafting workflow remains repository tooling for the same LEGO Star Wars GameCube reconstruction.

classification.narrative: The work is matching decompilation/reconstruction supported by Ghidra, REA and m2c-derived drafts.

source_cpu.narrative: The original GameCube executable remains PowerPC; PS2DMA function names describe engine subsystems rather than a newly evidenced source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The reconstruction target remains GameCube PowerPC as previously evidenced; host-side analysis tooling is not a target architecture.

build.narrative: Upstream integrates Ghidra/REA drafting, variant search, m2c drafts and finishable-unit ranking and reports matching six PS2DMA scratch/packet helpers.
build.limitations: The tracker did not configure the toolchain, compile the reconstruction or independently verify function matches.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed commits provide no minimum console revision, RAM, emulator, SDK or host requirement.
